assessment.chemometrics_note: NIR spectral bands overlap extensively, requiring chemometric regression (such as PLS) combined with scatter correction techniques like SNV or MSC to isolate protein concentration changes from physical turbidity fluctuations.
assessment.realtime_tracking_note: In-line NIR spectroscopy enables continuous real-time monitoring of protein concentration directly in the whey stream before concentration.
assessment.future_direction: Integration of cloud-based IoT sensor modules for remote tracking and automated process feedback.

proposal.what_would_change_it: If turbidity changes cause complete signal blockage in transflection mode, alternative configurations like MIR ATR or multi-method integration would be required.
proposal.next_step: Conduct laboratory feasibility trials using NIR transflection on representative clear and turbid whey samples against customer reference data.

assessment.brief_answer: To track protein concentration in a whey stream shifting between clear and turbid states, we recommend NIR spectroscopy using a transflection probe configuration. A fixed transmission setup would saturate under high turbidity, whereas a transflection approach accommodates varying optical path requirements. Feasibility trials should test representative samples across both states with chemometric scatter correction and laboratory reference comparison.
